transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-02-07
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Leila Park (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Alpine CTO), Ana Ruiz (Alpine ML Eng), Tom O'Neill (Alpine Head Security), Pri Henderson (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Alpine's model needs for claims automation (summarization + triage), discussion across hosted vs dedicated vs private, open-model comparisons, context length requirements for long claim threads, multilingual support (Spanish), tool-calling for external policy DB lookups, and security/KMS constraints. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC2 docs and scheduling a 2-week dedicated pilot with sample data.

Topics:
- current stack and infra (on-prem + AWS hybrid)
- primary use case: claims summarization + intent classification + tool-calling for policy lookups
- required context window: long threads up to ~25k tokens (attachments + chat history)
- multilingual: English + Spanish primarily, occasional Portuguese
- security: KMS/HSM, VPC peering, audit logs, retention policy
- cost vs latency tradeoffs and rollout plan

Action items (recap): see action_items field

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the account, Leila is our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Samir (Alpine CTO): Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Leila (Redwood SE): Quick agenda — understand your workflows, model selection needs, and constraints around security and deployment. Then propose pilot approach. Sound good?
[00:20] Pri (Product): Yep that's perfect. We want to get a sense of hosted vs dedicated, and whether we need private.
[00:28] Ana (ML Eng): Also we need concrete latency numbers — for our triage path we need sub-500ms for short responses, but longer summarizations can be higher. We'll talk about batching.
[00:36] Tom (Security): I want to flag KMS and audit log requirements up front. We have to pass a security questionnaire for any vendor.
[00:42] Jordan: Totally, we can cover that. Redwood has SOC 2, ISO — we also support customer-managed KMS and private VPC deployments.
[01:05] Speaker 1: (mumbles) sorry one sec, pulling up the doc...
[01:18] Leila: Can you describe the claim data shape? Attachments, OCR'd text, chat transcripts?
[01:25] Ana: Mostly OCR text from PDFs, email threads, and agent chat logs. Some scanned images with low-quality OCR so sequences can get long — a single claim can be many pages. We're estimating up to 25K tokens for full context.
[01:36] Jordan: 25K tokens, good to know. Our runtime supports model variants that do 8K, 32K and larger contexts — for hosted we have certain verified model profiles and for dedicated/private you can bring larger context models or tuned variants.
[01:54] Samir: Are these verified open models or Redwood models? What's in the catalog?
[01:59] Leila: Mostly curated open models and some Redwood-verified performance profiles. We tune kernel selection and quantization paths depending on the instance. For Alpine, we'd likely test 32k-capable open models first.
[02:20] Ana: We're also evaluating Anthropic and Cohere for accuracy on summarization. OpenAI is in the mix too. Any published evals we can see?
[02:30] Jordan: We'll share our benchmark sheets — latency and ROUGE/BLEU-ish metrics for common summarization prompts. Also we have eval runs for multilingual Spanish summarization for a few open models.
[02:42] Tom: On encryption, can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS and use customer-managed keys? We cannot have vendor-side keys for PII in pilot.
[02:52] Leila: Yes, customer KMS is supported in Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we offer bring-your-own-key in certain plans; we'll include the KMS checklist in the pack.
[03:05] Pri: If we go hosted to start, can we guarantee data isolation per-tenant?
[03:10] Jordan: Hosted has tenant isolation and RBAC; for stricter guarantees Dedicated gives GPU isolation and VPC peering. Private is the route if you need customer-managed control plane and on-prem.
[03:22] Samir: Cost is a big factor. We have to justify infra spend. If we do a dedicated pool, what's the typical commit and uplift for SLA?
[03:32] Leila: Dedicated is typically monthly or annual reserved capacity. We can size for your 95th percentile throughput and propose burst policies. We'll give cost estimates as a range depending on model choice and quantization.
[03:44] Ana: About quantization — do you recommend q4_0 or int8 for long-context models? We're worried about hallucinations with aggressive quant.
[03:53] Leila: For long-form summarization we tend to use q4_0 for a balance; some models take int8 and we validate QA. Part of the pilot is model/quantization recommendations and regression monitoring.
[04:07] Tom: Audit logs and retention — we need immutable logs for 6 months and the ability to search by token-level usage if necessary.
[04:16] Jordan: That's supported in the Console — token-level cost and latency breakdowns, and audit trails. We'll show examples in the security pack.
[04:30] Speaker 1: (overlap) can you also do tool-calling to our policy DB? That's critical for triage.
[04:36] Leila: Yes, function/tool calling is supported. We can wire a secure connector to your policy DB via a VPC peered connector. The flow includes authentication with short-lived creds.
[04:48] Ana: We need deterministic calls — if the model says to call policy A, we need to ensure the call happens programmatically, not a human interpretation.
[04:56] Leila: Absolutely; we support structured tool outputs and strict function schemas to avoid ambiguity.
[05:10] Samir: What about latency when calling tools? If the model needs to call external DB for each turn, that could blow up latency.
[05:18] Leila: We design for a hybrid — cache policy lookups when possible, and use async tool calls with progressive streaming. For low-latency triage, we recommend pre-caching common policy buckets.
[05:30] Pri: For Spanish support, which models do better? Our agents are bilingual and we need parity in quality.
[05:37] Leila: Some Llama-family and Mistral clones perform well, plus specialized Spanish-tuned forks. We'll propose a shortlist with multilingual evals.
[05:50] Ana: Cool. Any competitors we should be mindful of? We already talked to Anthropic and Cohere and are testing Vertex for auto-scaling.
[05:58] Jordan: Noted — we often see those. We'll include comparison notes and where Redwood's optimizations help cost/latency.
[06:12] Speaker 1: (typing) question: do you support private on-prem for PII-only workloads?
[06:18] Jordan: Yes, Private deployments give you the control plane and you can have an on-prem package. That said, onboarding time is longer — typically 6-12 weeks depending on integration complexity.
[06:31] Tom: That onboarding window is a challenge — we have a Q2 pilot target. If on-prem takes too long, we may start hosted/dedicated and then move to Private for production.
[06:42] Leila: That's a common path: hosted for quick iteration, dedicated for predictable throughput, and then private for strict compliance.
[06:52] Pri: For the 2-week pilot, what would success criteria look like?
[06:58] Ana: From ML: F1 > 0.78 on triage labels, summary ROUGE-L within 5 points of our human baseline. Latency under 2s for full-text summarization in the pilot. Security: keys remain customer-managed.
[07:12] Jordan: Good — we'll bake those into the pilot runbook.
[07:20] Samir: Do you support version pinning and can we rollback between model variants?
[07:26] Leila: Yes, rollout features include canary deploys, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin versions per route.
[07:36] Ana: One technical thing — our data is sharded across regions. Can Redwood route requests to different regions on policy? We want EU data to stay in EU.
[07:46] Jordan: Smart routing by region is supported — routing policies can keep requests in the desired region and fallback if capacity is constrained. We'll include region-specific latency numbers.
[07:58] Tom: Regarding audits, do you support exportable logs for internal SIEM ingestion? We need syslog/S3 export options.
[08:06] Leila: Yes, audit logs can be exported to S3 or Syslog sinks.
[08:12] Speaker 1: (whisper) sorry had a call echo, can you repeat the dedicated sizing part?
[08:21] Jordan: Sure — dedicated sizing is based on throughput targets; we estimate required GPU count and reserved capacity. For example, for 2k concurrent short queries we'll recommend a pool size X — we'll model it in the proposal.
[08:35] Ana: Do you have prebuilt connectors for our internal tools (ServiceNow, internal policy DB)?
[08:41] Leila: We have generic REST/webhook connectors and can build custom secure connectors as part of the pilot.
[08:50] Samir: Any limits or throttles on streaming responses? We might stream partial summaries to the UI.
[08:56] Leila: Streaming is supported and you can control chunk sizes and socket timeouts.
[09:06] Pri: Ok can we talk about costs briefly? Ballpark per 1M tokens for hosted vs dedicated?
[09:12] Jordan: Ballpark: hosted per-token costs vary by model — we'll give ranges. Dedicated reduces unit cost via reserved capacity. We'll send a pricing sheet.
[09:22] Ana: For the pilot, we want to exercise a 32k context model for a few large claims. Will that be expensive?
[09:29] Leila: Larger context windows do increase compute. We'll run a few sample billing sims in the pilot to show unit economics and recommend caching opportunities to reduce cost.
[09:40] Tom: On compliance, do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC per team? We need team-level access controls.
[09:47] Jordan: Yes, SSO, SAML, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls are standard.
[09:56] Speaker 1: (unclear) how do you handle KV cache invalidation for policy updates?
[10:02] Leila: Cache invalidation can be pushed via API; we also support TTLs and versioned keys for safe rollout.
[10:12] Ana: Are there any known failure modes where the model's tool-calling could be skipped and lead to incorrect triage? We need guardrails.
[10:20] Leila: We implement strict schema enforcement and can set up a verification step that checks required function outputs and retries or fails closed.
[10:31] Samir: For long-term operations, how do model updates work? We don't want drift in production.
[10:38] Jordan: Redwood Optimize monitors quality and can alert on regressions tied to prompt sets. You can pin a model and schedule controlled rollouts.
[10:48] Pri: Good. Any legal/licensing issues for using certain open models in insurance?
[10:53] Jordan: That depends on model license — we'll flag any concerns in the shortlist. If you need non-commercial or particular terms, we'll surface that.
[11:04] Speaker 1: (background) is there a sample SLA for downtime?
[11:09] Jordan: Dedicated includes SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, hosted has standard terms. We'll include the SLA PDF.
[11:18] Ana: For the sample data, we can anonymize and share 5 claims. Are there any formatting expectations?
[11:24] Leila: CSV or JSON with text chunks is fine. If you want, we can provide a template.
[11:30] Tom: About on-prem private deployment — what's the required network topology? Do you need incoming connections or do you pull updates?
[11:39] Leila: Typically the private package can be deployed behind your firewall; control plane connections can be configured via customer-managed channels. We'll include network diagrams.
[11:52] Samir: If we move from hosted to private, do we get continuity on model versions and evals?
[11:58] Jordan: Yes, we migrate config and model pin metadata; actual model binaries and hosting are arranged per deployment.
[12:09] Pri: For tool-calling, can we have a dry-run mode that logs intended calls without executing? That would help for compliance.
[12:17] Leila: We can instrument a dry-run where function outputs are logged but not executed; useful for testing.
[12:27] Ana: Great. Any recommended open models for Spanish summarization we should try first?
[12:33] Leila: We'll propose 3: a 32k-capable Llama fork tuned for summarization, a Mistral clone with Spanish fine-tuning, and a smaller low-latency multilingual model. We'll include eval metrics.
[12:46] Samir: How do we measure hallucination risk in the pilot? We need automated checks.
[12:52] Leila: Redwood Optimize can run reference-based and reference-free checks; we'll set up hallucination detection tied to thresholds and alerts.
[13:02] Speaker 1: (murmur) okay where do we sign up for the trial?
[13:07] Jordan: We'll send a pilot agreement. For the trial you'll get dedicated nodes for the two-week window and a runbook.
[13:16] Tom: On logging, we need token-level attribution for auditing — can you export per-request token breakdowns?
[13:22] Leila: Yup — the Console provides per-request token counts and cost attributions; exports are possible.
[13:30] Ana: For the pilot, we also want example prompts and prompt templates for the summarizer and triage.
[13:36] Jordan: We'll include prompt templates and suggested evaluation harness.
[13:42] Pri: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[13:47] Leila: Only that long context models are more compute-heavy and may need caching strategies. Also private deployments take longer.
[13:55] Samir: Ok let's align timeline — pilot in mid-February?
[14:00] Jordan: We can start the pilot week of Feb 13 if data is ready. That fits your Q2 runway.
[14:08] Ana: I'll start prepping and ping Tom for the security bits.
[14:12] Tom: I'll send the questionnaire after the call.
[14:16] Jordan: Great. We'll send the security pack and pilot doc.
[14:20] Speaker 1: (overlap) thanks all.
[14:23] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[14:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of "KV cache"), speaker 1 labelled where camera audio was fuzzy. Natural speech patterns and interruptions preserved.
